- When sentiment turns positive (≥0.5) after a recent dip, model tends to overreact and overshoot upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤-0.5) after a recent spike, model underreacts — increase forecast decline slope to match sentiment intensity.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — add 2–3% bias upward for first 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (≥10% from prior 7-day avg), model often fails to capture continuation — extend forecast horizon with slight downward bias to reflect mean reversion.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +1/-1 cycles, model tends to lag by 1–2 days — adjust forecast to align with sentiment reversal timing.
- For 30-day forecasts, model overestimates late-period prices (days 20–30) when sentiment is neutral — reduce final 5–7 days by 3–5% to avoid overconfidence in tail behavior.
